# kaiten_deployment_zone (Resource)

Manages a Kaiten deployment zone: a region or environment that instances are deployed to.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "kaiten_deployment_zone" "eu_west" {
  name        = "AWS eu-west-1"
  slug        = "aws-eu-west-1"
  type        = "production"
  description = "Primary production region for EU customers."

  metadata = jsonencode({
    region = "eu-west-1"
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable name of the deployment zone, e.g. `AWS us-west-2`.
- `type` (String) Environment class of the deployment zone. Free-form, but `production`, `staging` and `development` are the values the Kaiten console labels, and feature-flag targeting rules match on it as `__kaiten.deploymentZone.type`.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the deployment zone. Defaults to an empty string.
- `metadata` (String) Metadata of the deployment zone, as a JSON-encoded object. Kaiten validates it against the metadata fields the organization declares for deployment zones. Use `jsonencode()` to build it. Removing it clears the zone's metadata.
- `release_id` (String) ID of the release currently deployed to the zone. Setting or changing it records a deployment of that release in the zone's history. When omitted, Terraform leaves the release alone, so deployments made outside Terraform are not reverted.
- `slug` (String) URL-friendly identifier of the deployment zone, unique within the organization. Generated from `name` when omitted. A slug cannot be renamed: changing it replaces the deployment zone.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the deployment zone was created, in RFC 3339 format.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier (UUID) of the deployment zone, assigned by Kaiten.
- `updated_at` (String) When the deployment zone was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = kaiten_deployment_zone.eu_west
  id = "aws-eu-west-1"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A deployment zone is imported by its slug.
terraform import kaiten_deployment_zone.eu_west aws-eu-west-1
```
